ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
An open electrical circuit contains a wire loop in the shape of a semi-circle, that contains a resistor of resistance $R=0.2 \Omega$. The circuit is completed by a conducting pendulum in the form of a uniform rod with length $\ell=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $m=0.05 \mathrm{~kg}$, has no resistance, and stays in contact with the other wires at all times. All electrical components are oriented in the $y z$ plane, and gravity acts in the $z$ direction. A constant magnetic field of strength $B=2 \mathrm{~T}$ is applied in the $+x$ direction.
<image_1>

Ignoring self inductance and assuming that $\alpha \ll 1$, the general equation of motion is in the form of $\theta(t)=A(t) \cos (\omega t+\varphi)$, where $A(t) \geq 0$. Find $\omega^{2}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The circuit in the figure lies in the plane of the paper, and its shape is a semicircular guide rail, with a section of wire containing resistor R above. The length of the conducting rod is marked as ℓ; one end contacts the pivot near the upper wire, and the other end contacts the semicircular arc guide rail. The angle between the rod and the vertical dashed line is marked as α. The many dotted circles in the figure indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the paper and outward; the arrow g on the right indicates gravity downward. The structure in the figure is consistent with the meaning of the problem: the conducting rod serves as a pendulum rod to close the circuit, and the semicircular guide rail and the resistor form the loop. Reasoning: The conducting rod rotates about the upper end and produces motional electromotive force in the uniform magnetic field B perpendicular to the plane of the loop. The speed of a small segment of the rod at distance r from the rotation axis is r θdot, so the electromotive force is ε = ∫_0^ℓ B r θdot dr = (1/2)Bℓ^2 θdot. The rod has no resistance and self-inductance is neglected, so the current I = ε/R = Bℓ^2 θdot/(2R). The magnetic field produces an opposite damping torque on the current-carrying rod, whose magnitude is τ_B = ∫_0^ℓ r I B dr = (1/2)IBℓ^2 = B^2ℓ^4 θdot/(4R), with direction opposing the motion. The moment of inertia of a uniform rod about an endpoint is I_rod = mℓ^2/3. Under small angles, the gravitational restoring torque is τ_g ≈ -mg(ℓ/2)θ. Therefore the equation of motion is (mℓ^2/3) θddot + (B^2ℓ^4/(4R)) θdot + mgℓθ/2 = 0. Dividing by mℓ^2/3 gives θddot + β θdot + ω_0^2 θ = 0, where β = 3B^2ℓ^2/(4mR), ω_0^2 = 3g/(2ℓ). Substituting B=2 T, ℓ=0.1 m, m=0.05 kg, R=0.2 Ω, g=9.8 m/s^2: β = 3×4×0.01/(4×0.05×0.2)=3, ω_0^2 = 3×9.8/(2×0.1)=147. The angular frequency of the underdamped oscillation satisfies ω^2 = ω_0^2 - β^2/4 = 147 - 9/4 = 144.75, approximately 145.

raw_record.question_text:
An open electrical circuit contains a wire loop in the shape of a semi-circle, that contains a resistor of resistance $R=0.2 \Omega$. The circuit is completed by a conducting pendulum in the form of a uniform rod with length $\ell=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $m=0.05 \mathrm{~kg}$, has no resistance, and stays in contact with the other wires at all times. All electrical components are oriented in the $yz$ plane, and gravity acts in the $z$ direction. A constant magnetic field of strength $B=2 \mathrm{~T}$ is applied in the $+x$ direction.

Ignoring self inductance and assuming that $\alpha \ll 1$, the general equation of motion is in the form of $\theta(t)=A(t)\cos(\omega t+\varphi)$, where $A(t)\geq 0$. Find $\omega^2$.

method.method_draft: Direct equation-of-motion route. First read the image: the rod is a radial conducting pendulum of length ℓ inside a semicircular rail in the yz-plane, making a small angle α or θ from the downward dashed vertical; the field is shown by dots as out of the page, matching +x, and gravity points downward. Read from the text the values R=0.2 Ω, ℓ=0.1 m, m=0.05 kg, B=2 T, and that the rod has no resistance and self-inductance is ignored. Use the semicircular/radial geometry to write the motional emf of a rotating rod in a perpendicular uniform magnetic field: ε = ∫0^ℓ B r θdot dr = (1/2)Bℓ^2 θdot. Hence I=ε/R. The magnetic force on each element gives an opposing torque τB = ∫0^ℓ r I B dr = (1/2)IBℓ^2 = (B^2ℓ^4/(4R))θdot. The gravitational torque for a uniform rod about its upper contact is τg≈-mg(ℓ/2)θ, and the moment of inertia is Irod=mℓ^2/3. Therefore mℓ^2/3 θddot + B^2ℓ^4/(4R) θdot + mgℓ/2 θ = 0. Identify the damped oscillator parameters β = [B^2ℓ^4/(4R)]/[mℓ^2/3] = 3B^2ℓ^2/(4mR) and ω0^2 = [mgℓ/2]/[mℓ^2/3] = 3g/(2ℓ). Since θ(t)=A(t)cos(ωt+φ), use ω^2=ω0^2-β^2/4. Substituting B=2, ℓ=0.1, m=0.05, R=0.2, g=9.8 gives β=3 and ω^2=147-2.25=144.75≈145.

推理：导体杆绕上端转动，在垂直于回路平面的匀强磁场 B 中产生动生电动势。杆上距转轴 r 的小段速度为 r θdot，因此电动势为 ε = ∫_0^ℓ B r θdot dr = (1/2)Bℓ^2 θdot。杆无电阻且忽略自感，所以电流 I = ε/R = Bℓ^2 θdot/(2R)。磁场对电流杆产生反向阻尼力矩，其大小为 τ_B = ∫_0^ℓ r I B dr = (1/2)IBℓ^2 = B^2ℓ^4 θdot/(4R)，方向反抗运动。均匀杆绕端点的转动惯量为 I_rod = mℓ^2/3。小角度下重力回复力矩为 τ_g ≈ -mg(ℓ/2)θ。因此运动方程为 (mℓ^2/3) θddot + (B^2ℓ^4/(4R)) θdot + mgℓθ/2 = 0。除以 mℓ^2/3，得 θddot + β θdot + ω_0^2 θ = 0，其中 β = 3B^2ℓ^2/(4mR)，ω_0^2 = 3g/(2ℓ)。代入 B=2 T，ℓ=0.1 m，m=0.05 kg，R=0.2 Ω，g=9.8 m/s^2：β = 3×4×0.01/(4×0.05×0.2)=3，ω_0^2 = 3×9.8/(2×0.1)=147。欠阻尼振荡的角频率满足 ω^2 = ω_0^2 - β^2/4 = 147 - 9/4 = 144.75，约为 145。

method.method_draft: Energy/flux-damping route. First read the image: the rod sweeps out a circular sector inside the semicircular loop as it rotates by θ about the upper contact; the resistor lies in the fixed wire path, and the field dots indicate uniform B perpendicular to the loop. Read from the text R=0.2 Ω, ℓ=0.1 m, m=0.05 kg, B=2 T, no rod resistance, and small α. Use the image geometry to get the changing circuit area: for small changes in θ, Asector=(1/2)ℓ^2 θ, so the magnetic flux is Φ=B(1/2)ℓ^2 θ. Faraday’s law gives |ε|=(Bℓ^2/2)|θdot| and the resistor dissipates power P=ε^2/R=(B^2ℓ^4/(4R))θdot^2. Interpret this as viscous rotational damping, since P=c θdot^2, so c=B^2ℓ^4/(4R). The mechanical energy of the uniform rod near vertical is E=(1/2)(mℓ^2/3)θdot^2+(1/2)(mgℓ/2)θ^2. The Lagrange equation with Rayleigh dissipation cθdot gives mℓ^2/3 θddot + c θdot + mgℓ/2 θ=0. Thus β=c/(mℓ^2/3)=3B^2ℓ^2/(4mR) and ω0^2=3g/(2ℓ). Then the oscillatory factor has ω^2=ω0^2-β^2/4 = 147-2.25≈145.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中显示一个位于竖直平面内的半圆形固定导线回路，顶部固定导线中串有电阻 R。一个长度为 ℓ 的导体棒从上方接触点斜向下接触半圆弧，棒与竖直虚线之间的夹角标为 α。图中许多带点圆圈表示均匀磁场垂直于回路平面，右侧箭头表示重力向下。导体棒转动时会扫过以其上端接触点为圆心、半径为 ℓ 的圆形扇形面积。

推理：令小角位移为 θ。由图像几何，棒转过小角 θ 时，电路包围面积的变化为扇形面积 A = (1/2)ℓ^2 θ，因此磁通量 Φ = B A = (Bℓ^2/2)θ。忽略自感，感应电动势大小为 ε = |dΦ/dt| = (Bℓ^2/2)|θdot|。电阻中耗散功率为 P = ε^2/R = (B^2ℓ^4/(4R))θdot^2。把它写成转动粘滞阻尼功率 P = c θdot^2，得 c = B^2ℓ^4/(4R)。

均匀棒绕端点转动的转动惯量 I = mℓ^2/3。小角度下重力势能近似为 (1/2)(mgℓ/2)θ^2，所以回复力矩常数 k = mgℓ/2。运动方程为 I θddot + c θdot + k θ = 0，即 θddot + β θdot + ω0^2 θ = 0，其中 β = c/I = 3B^2ℓ^2/(4mR)，ω0^2 = k/I = 3g/(2ℓ)。

代入 B = 2 T，ℓ = 0.1 m，m = 0.05 kg，R = 0.2 Ω：β = 3(2^2)(0.1^2)/(4·0.05·0.2) = 3 s^-1。取 g = 9.8 m/s^2，ω0^2 = 3(9.8)/(2·0.1) = 147 s^-2。欠阻尼振荡因子中的角频率满足 ω^2 = ω0^2 - β^2/4 = 147 - 9/4 = 144.75 ≈ 145。

图像描述：图中显示一个位于竖直平面内的半圆形固定导线回路，顶部固定导线中串有电阻 R。一个长度为 ℓ 的导体棒从上方接触点斜向下接触半圆弧，棒与竖直虚线之间的夹角标为 α。图中许多带点圆圈表示均匀磁场垂直于回路平面，右侧箭头表示重力向下。导体棒转动时会扫过以其上端接触点为圆心、半径为 ℓ 的圆形扇形面积。

推理：令小角位移为 θ。由图像几何，棒转过小角 θ 时，电路包围面积的变化为扇形面积 A = (1/2)ℓ^2 θ，因此磁通量 Φ = B A = (Bℓ^2/2)θ。忽略自感，感应电动势大小为 ε = |dΦ/dt| = (Bℓ^2/2)|θdot|。电阻中耗散功率为 P = ε^2/R = (B^2ℓ^4/(4R))θdot^2。把它写成转动粘滞阻尼功率 P = c θdot^2，得 c = B^2ℓ^4/(4R)。

均匀棒绕端点转动的转动惯量 I = mℓ^2/3。小角度下重力势能近似为 (1/2)(mgℓ/2)θ^2，所以回复力矩常数 k = mgℓ/2。运动方程为 I θddot + c θdot + k θ = 0，即 θddot + β θdot + ω0^2 θ = 0，其中 β = c/I = 3B^2ℓ^2/(4mR)，ω0^2 = k/I = 3g/(2ℓ)。

代入 B = 2 T，ℓ = 0.1 m，m = 0.05 kg，R = 0.2 Ω：β = 3(2^2)(0.1^2)/(4·0.05·0.2) = 3 s^-1。取 g = 9.8 m/s^2，ω0^2 = 3(9.8)/(2·0.1) = 147 s^-2。欠阻尼振荡因子中的角频率满足 ω^2 = ω0^2 - β^2/4 = 147 - 9/4 = 144.75 ≈ 145。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This route avoids computing the magnetic force distribution directly; it obtains the electromagnetic effect from changing flux and Joule power, then maps the power loss to a Rayleigh damping coefficient.
planner_metadata.image_role: The image is used to identify the swept sector area of a radial rod in a semicircular loop, the resistor as the dissipative element in the fixed circuit, the vertical equilibrium reference line, and the perpendicular magnetic field direction.
planner_metadata.text_role: The text provides the physical parameters, confirms that self-inductance can be ignored so current follows ε/R instantly, and states the small-angle form needed to linearize the pendulum energy.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Uses Faraday’s law via changing flux area, Joule heating P=ε²/R, equivalence of rotational viscous damping power P=cθdot², small-angle gravitational potential for a uniform rod, and the damped harmonic oscillator frequency formula.

raw_record.original_question:
An open electrical circuit contains a wire loop in the shape of a semi-circle, that contains a resistor of resistance $R=0.2 \Omega$. The circuit is completed by a conducting pendulum in the form of a uniform rod with length $\ell=0.1 \mathrm{~m}$ and mass $m=0.05 \mathrm{~kg}$, has no resistance, and stays in contact with the other wires at all times. All electrical components are oriented in the $yz$ plane, and gravity acts in the $z$ direction. A constant magnetic field of strength $B=2 \mathrm{~T}$ is applied in the $+x$ direction.

Ignoring self inductance and assuming that $\alpha \ll 1$, the general equation of motion is in the form of $\theta(t)=A(t)\cos(\omega t+\varphi)$, where $A(t)\geq 0$. Find $\omega^2$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The circuit in the figure lies in the plane of the paper, and its shape is a semicircular guide rail, with a section of wire containing resistor R above. The length of the conducting rod is marked as ℓ; one end contacts the pivot near the upper wire, and the other end contacts the semicircular arc guide rail. The angle between the rod and the vertical dashed line is marked as α. The many dotted circles in the figure indicate that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the paper and outward; the arrow g on the right indicates gravity downward. The structure in the figure is consistent with the meaning of the problem: the conducting rod serves as a pendulum rod to close the circuit, and the semicircular guide rail and the resistor form the loop.

Reasoning: The conducting rod rotates about the upper end and produces motional electromotive force in the uniform magnetic field B perpendicular to the plane of the loop. The speed of a small segment of the rod at distance r from the rotation axis is r θdot, so the electromotive force is ε = ∫_0^ℓ B r θdot dr = (1/2)Bℓ^2 θdot. The rod has no resistance and self-inductance is neglected, so the current I = ε/R = Bℓ^2 θdot/(2R). The magnetic field produces an opposite damping torque on the current-carrying rod, whose magnitude is τ_B = ∫_0^ℓ r I B dr = (1/2)IBℓ^2 = B^2ℓ^4 θdot/(4R), with direction opposing the motion. The moment of inertia of a uniform rod about an endpoint is I_rod = mℓ^2/3. Under small angles, the gravitational restoring torque is τ_g ≈ -mg(ℓ/2)θ. Therefore the equation of motion is (mℓ^2/3) θddot + (B^2ℓ^4/(4R)) θdot + mgℓθ/2 = 0. Dividing by mℓ^2/3 gives θddot + β θdot + ω_0^2 θ = 0, where β = 3B^2ℓ^2/(4mR), ω_0^2 = 3g/(2ℓ). Substituting B=2 T, ℓ=0.1 m, m=0.05 kg, R=0.2 Ω, g=9.8 m/s^2: β = 3×4×0.01/(4×0.05×0.2)=3, ω_0^2 = 3×9.8/(2×0.1)=147. The angular frequency of the underdamped oscillation satisfies ω^2 = ω_0^2 - β^2/4 = 147 - 9/4 = 144.75, approximately 145.
